knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Shift and Stretch Applied to an Exponential Growth Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087824/plots/shift-stretch-v5/bb1645b22a5dfa6dcdb4ce73904109d1f4b2dd2451f9becdb0e69907cce6035b.png)

The graph above shows $y=k({4}^{x})+c.$ Find the value of $k$ and $c.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k({4}^{x})+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=4,$ so $c=4.$

Therefore, our function takes the form

$$
y=k({4}^{x})+4.
$$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ The labeled point on the graph is $(0,6),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=6$ into the function and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =k({4}^{x})+4 \\ 6 & =k({4}^{0})+4 \\ 6 & =k(1)+4 \\ 6 & =k+4 \\ 2 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k=2$ and $c=4.$

$$
y=k({2}^{x})-3.
